candidate_inputs.text:
HTTP cache validation
An origin server can attach an ETag to a response as an opaque identifier for that version of the resource. A cache sends the saved ETag in If-None-Match when validating the resource. If the selected representation still matches, the server can return 304 Not Modified without a response body, and the cache reuses its stored body. An ETag is not necessarily a content hash. Cache freshness determines whether a stored response can be reused without validation; validation checks whether a stored representation is still usable.

Learn the complete set:
- A: maps a hostname to an IPv4 address.
- AAAA: maps a hostname to an IPv6 address.
- CNAME: aliases one DNS name to another DNS name.
